claim: Gaomei Wetlands is about 45 minutes from Taichung city center; reach it by train to Qingshui (45 min) then bus 178/179 (20 min), and arrive a good hour or two before sunset; visit at low tide to see intertidal life.
quote: Gaomei sits approximately 45 minutes from Taichung's city center... Take the regular train from Taichung Station to Qingshui (45 minutes)... use Bus 178 or 179 (20 minutes)... Arrive a good hour or two before sunset

claim: Gaomei Wetlands features an 800-meter boardwalk over a 300+ hectare wetland with 18 coastal wind turbines (each 64m tall) forming a 'Wind Turbine Avenue' that silhouettes the sunset; boardwalk closes 3-4 hours around high tide so check the tide table.
quote: 18 wind turbines, each 64 meters tall... form what locals and tourists call the Wind Turbine Avenue... 800-meter dock... Due to high tide, the closure will take 3 to 4 hours.

claim: Sun Moon Lake is reachable from Taichung by Nantou Bus 6670 in 90 minutes from Taichung HSR or 2 hours from Taichung TRA station, running roughly every 30 minutes; ticket is TWD 197 one-way / TWD 360 return, making it doable as a day trip.
quote: The Taiwan Tourist Shuttle bus from Nantou Bus... from either Taichung HSR (1.5 hours) or Taichung TRA Station (2 hours)... TWD 197 for a single trip and TWD 360 for a return trip... last bus back to Taichung departing from Sun Moon Lake at 7:25PM

claim: Wuling Farm is far from Taichung: about 3 hours by car, or roughly 6 hours by bus, making it impractical for a weekend already anchored by a dinner.
quote: The fastest way to get from Taichung to Wuling Farm is to drive which takes 3 hours... The cheapest way is by bus which costs $2-$5 and takes 6 hours 5 minutes.

claim: Wuling Farm / Hehuanshan is a high-altitude alpine destination known for cherry blossoms (Feb-March), summer stargazing and high-mountain hiking, and one of Taiwan's most famous (though not guaranteed) snow spots at Hehuanshan in Jan-Feb.
quote: Hehuanshan is one of the easiest and most famous places to see snow in Taiwan, with snow sometimes falling there in January or February, but it's never guaranteed... Peak season for cherry blossoms runs from February through March 2026

claim: Lihpao Land theme park is about 23 minutes (14 miles) by car from Taichung, or reachable by slow train to Houli Station then a free hourly shuttle, or bus line 155 (about 56 min).
quote: The driving distance between Taichung to Lihpao Land is 14 miles. It takes approximately 23 min to drive... Catch the slow train to Houli Station, then take the free shuttle that runs hourly... line 155 bus which takes 56 min

claim: The Hou-Feng (Houfeng) Bike Path runs 4.5km from Fengyuan under National Highway 4, through Tunnel No.9 and across the Dajia River Steel Bridge to Houli Horse Ranch, and connects to the Dongfeng Green Way for an 18km route.
quote: The Hou-Fong bike path starts under the elevated bridge of National Highway No. 4, passing Tunnel No.9 and Dajia River Steel Bridge, and ends in Houli Horse Ranch. The total length of the bikeway is 4.5 kilometers... connected to Dongfeng Bicycle Green Way... 18 kilometers

claim: Reach Houfeng Bikeway by train from Taichung to Fengyuan (20 minutes) and rent a bike (around TWD 300) outside the station; a round-trip ride takes about 1-2 hours.
quote: take a train from Taichung to Fengyuan (20 minutes) then rent a bike here outside the station... Bike rentals are available on-site at an affordable price of TWD300. Round trip cycling time takes about 1 to 2 hours.

claim: Dakeng Scenic Area, a short drive from Taichung, has 10 official trails: numbers 1-5 are longer and more challenging while 6-10 are closer to town and easier; arrive by 7:00-7:30am and reach it by car/Uber or Taichung Bus Line 66 (Dakeng Loop).
quote: Number 1 to 5 are the ones that are more challenging and longer. Number 6 to 10 are closer to town and easier... get there by 7:00 - 7:30 AM... transfer to Taichung Bus Line 66 (Dakeng Loop)

claim: Dakeng's Trail No.4 is the most challenging, featuring a famous near-vertical 300-meter wooden-log slope nicknamed the 'soft foot slope', and as of January 2026 it is closed indefinitely for construction and repair.
quote: Trail 4 is particularly challenging—the most difficult because there is a 300-meter-long, nearly vertical steep slope that is nicknamed the 'soft foot slope'... As of January 2026, the Dakeng No. 4 Trail is closed due to extensive construction and repair work.

claim: Lukang Old Street in Changhua is a well-preserved traditional town reachable from Taichung HSR by Changhua bus 6936 in about 50 minutes, or bus 9018 direct from Taichung Railway Station in about 1.5 hours; busiest and best on weekends, avoid Mondays.
quote: Take Changhua bus 6936 and get off at Lukang Station. This bus takes about 50 minutes... Bus 9018 goes directly from Taichung to Lukang, taking 1.5 hours... avoid Mondays, when many things are closed.
